problem: The sentence 'Some orders may be weak or absent when the single-slit pattern puts a minimum there; one mention is enough' contains an editorial instruction ('one mention is enough') addressed to the writer, not the student, and it leaves the missing-order idea half-explained.
fix: Delete the editorial phrase and state the condition: an order m is missing when it falls on a single-slit minimum at the same angle, which happens when d/a = m/n (n = 1, 2, … is the order of the slit minimum).

where: Section 2 and Exam traps, m_max formula
problem: m_max = floor(d/λ) is stated without the edge case. When d/λ is exactly an integer, the order m = d/λ gives sin θ = 1, that is θ = 90°, a grazing beam that is not seen in practice, so the formula then overcounts by one.
fix: Add: m_max is the largest integer strictly less than d/λ; if d/λ is a whole number, that order sits at 90° and is not observed, so take m_max = d/λ − 1.
